add codex handoff document

Capture the current backend state, demo workflow, OpenAI browser-auth notes, and highest-priority next steps in a dedicated handoff document for a new Codex CLI session.

add bola and bfla demo coverage

Expand the vulnerable demo target and demo runner to exercise BOLA/tenant-isolation and BFLA flows, and adjust replay assertions so the backend can confirm those core vulnerability classes during the local autonomous pentest demo.

add scan inspection helper

Add a small backend inspection helper so demo runs can be explained from planner history, hypotheses, verifier jobs, findings, orchestration sessions, and runtime events instead of looking like a black box.

map verifier findings to real vuln categories

Use the job vulnerability class as the finding category during verifier execution so demo and report outputs reflect the real detected class like sqli or ssrf instead of generic business logic labels.

fallback cleanly when ai planner is rate limited

Keep autonomous sessions running when the AI planner is unavailable or rate limited by recording a failed AI planning step, updating memory so the loop can move on, and continuing into deterministic verification work instead of aborting the scan.

use local callback bridge for openai plus auth

Switch OpenAI browser auth to the localhost:1455 callback pattern used by the official Codex flow and add a local callback bridge that forwards the authorization code into the backend so ChatGPT Plus/Pro login works more like OpenCode.

allow demo runner to choose ai provider

Let the local demo pentest script target a specific AI provider so real OpenAI browser-auth demos can be exercised without editing the script by hand.

add real openai plus browser auth path

Implement a provider-specific OpenAI browser auth flow based on the official ChatGPT Plus/Pro to Codex backend pattern, store exchanged OAuth tokens securely, and resolve that auth path into a real planning provider instead of treating browser auth as a generic placeholder.

add vulnerable demo target and pentest runner

Add an intentionally vulnerable local API plus a demo runner that bootstraps a scan, ingests observed traffic, and starts autonomous orchestration so the backend can be demonstrated end-to-end on a local target.

add provider auth abstraction

Implement DB-backed AI provider configs with encrypted secret storage, auth method abstraction for API key, browser/OAuth scaffolding, and cloud credentials, then wire provider resolution toward OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI-compatible backends.

add one-shot scan setup and runtime profiles

Let users provide target base URL, actor profiles, source code, and API specs in one setup request so the backend can bootstrap a scan and start autonomous execution with per-scan replay configuration instead of relying on manual multi-step setup.

add migration for hypothesis lifecycle fields

Backfill the database migration chain so the persisted hypothesis lifecycle model stays aligned with the current backend schema, including canonical grouping, transition tracking, and stale-cycle state.

evolve hypotheses and memory across agent loops

Add automatic hypothesis merge, reopen, downgrade, and abandonment behavior, enrich orchestration memory with dead-end and follow-up summaries, and let autonomous sessions run remediation/report subloops after confirmations so the agent loop behaves more like a real pentester workflow over time.

persist hypotheses and ai-driven verification focus

Add first-class orchestration hypotheses with lifecycle states, let AI choose which hypothesis to verify next plus payload preference, and feed that state back into autonomous session memory so the agent loop can pursue, reprioritize, and trace work more like a real pentester.

let ai choose orchestration next actions

Extend the provider-neutral AI layer so autonomous sessions can ask an AI planner to choose the next action from persisted memory, while keeping deterministic fallback logic for resilience and traceable pentest execution.

make orchestration choose actions from memory

Move autonomous sessions away from a mostly fixed planner-then-verifier sequence by recording memory-driven decision steps and selecting the next action from current proxy observations, planning results, and pending verifier work.

build autonomous orchestration session layer

Add persisted orchestration sessions, step traces, and memory snapshots so a scan can run a real autonomous loop across deterministic planning, optional AI planning, and repeated verifier cycles from a single backend entrypoint.

add scan comparison and finding drift reports

Compare findings between two scan runs so teams can track new, resolved, changed, and unchanged issues over time and review drift directly from backend report APIs.

add structured exploit payload libraries

Introduce reusable replay payload variants for SQLi, SSRF, XSS, and authz classes so the verifier can try richer exploit families per finding instead of relying on one hard-coded mutation path.

add browser-assisted callback verification

Support headless browser execution for DOM/XSS-style verification, enrich callback analysis with fingerprints and metadata scoring, and thread callback-aware assertions through replay so SSRF and XSS confirmation can use out-of-band evidence instead of status codes alone.

add callback verification and taint correlation

Add out-of-band callback capture for SSRF and browser-style XSS confirmation, generate callback-aware replay plans, and deepen source artifact review with taint-style source/sink correlation so exploit hypotheses rely on stronger code evidence.

add replay assertions and response analyzers

Add replay assertion support for SQLi, SSRF, XSS, and cross-actor authorization drift, then use those analyzers during HTTP replay so verifier outcomes behave more like a professional pentest workflow instead of relying only on status codes.

add technical attack coverage and replay mutations

Introduce first-class SQLi, SSRF, and stored/reflected XSS rule coverage, deepen source/spec artifact analysis for exploit hypotheses, and extend replay plans with query, body, actor, and refresh-aware mutation logic to move the backend closer to professional pentest workflows.

strengthen replay verifier mutation engine

Add path and body mutation support, role and permission overrides, per-request actor switching, and refresh-driven retry logic so the verifier replay path moves closer to a professional pentester workflow for multi-step API abuse testing.

expand vulnerability coverage engine

Add explicit planner rule packs for BOLA/IDOR, BFLA, tenant isolation, mass assignment, excessive data exposure, and unsafe destructive actions, then thread coverage metadata into planner outputs, workflow contracts, and verifier job payloads.

chore: add test commit marker

Add a minimal marker file to verify the repository commit and push workflow without touching project code or personal untracked files.
